questions.qtext: In the Entity-Relationship (ER) model, what is the cardinality ratio that represents a relationship where each entity instance in one entity set is associated with exactly one entity instance in another entity set?
questions.solution:
(a)
In a 1 : 1 relationship, each entity instance in one entity set is associated with exactly one entity instance in another entity set.

questions.qtext: In the relational model, what does normalization refer to?

options.text: Storing data in a structured format for efficient retrieval
Removing redundant data from a database to improve data integrity
Breaking down large tables into smaller, more manageable tables
Organizing data into a hierarchy of directories for efficient storage

questions.solution:
(b)
Normalization in the relational model involves organizing data to reduce redundancy and
dependency, thereby improving data integrity.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is/are true from the statement about normal forms?

options.text: Lossless join and dependency preserving decomposition into 3NF is always possible.
Lossless join and dependency preserving decomposition into BCNF is always possible.
Any relation with two attribute is in 4NF.

questions.solution:
(a, c, d)
(a) Lossless join and dependency preserving decomposition into 3NF is always possible. True
(b) Lossless join and dependency preserving decomposition into BCNF may or may not possible.
False
(c) Two attribute relation like R(A, B) satisfied are normal form: 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF, 4NF, 5NF, 6NF. True
(d) BCNF is stronger than 3NF. True
